citation: Shpitser and Pearl (2006), Identification of Conditional Interventional Distributions, UAI-06, Figure 1, Sections 5-6, Figure 3, and Theorems 6-8
paper_status_note: Figure 3 IDC is the operative algorithm. Theorem 3 and Corollary 2 repeat the arbitrary-subquery hedge criterion later corrected by Shpitser (2023); they are not used as status tests.

a.reported_claim: P_x(Y) is not identifiable, while P_x(Y|Z) is identifiable because Rule 2 exchanges observation of Z for intervention on Z
a.adjudicated_claim: Rule 2 moves Z and exact ID of P_{x,z}(Y) succeeds; the strict-subquery hedge for P_x(Y) must not be promoted to a failure of the requested conditional query

b.reported_claim: P_x(Y) is identifiable and equal to P(Y), while conditioning on Z makes P_x(Y|Z) nonidentifiable
b.adjudicated_claim: The incoming edge Y -> Z is retained by G_{bar X, underline Z}, so Z is not moved; exact ID of P_x(Y,Z) returns a hedge

c.reported_claim: P_x(W|Z) is nonidentifiable and is a counterexample to the soundness of Tian's conditional-effect algorithm
c.adjudicated_claim: Z remains observed and exact ID of P_x(W,Z) returns the X-Z hedge
